objectives: Explain why multiple heads beat one big head

slides.title: Part 1 — Why one head is not enough
slides.body: Self-attention produces exactly one softmax distribution per query token. Language needs several relations resolved *at the same position, at the same time*. That tension is the entire motivation for multiple heads.

slides.title: One softmax = one relation
slides.body: A single attention head outputs, for query token $i$, one weighting over keys — it can express precisely **one** way of relating $i$ to the rest. But consider "The keys to the cabinets **are** on the table": at "are", the model must *simultaneously* track subject–verb agreement (→ "keys", to choose *are* vs *is*) **and** any coreference/locative structure. One head, one weighting, cannot encode both relations for the same query. You need several attentions running in parallel, each free to specialize.

slides.title: Run attention h times in parallel — the construction
slides.body: Multi-head attention splits the model dimension $d_{model}$ into $h$ subspaces of size $d_k=d_{model}/h$. For head $t$: project with its own $W^Q_t,W^K_t,W^V_t\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{model}\times d_k}$, run scaled dot-product attention, get an $n\times d_k$ output. Concatenate the $h$ head outputs back to $n\times d_{model}$ and mix with one output projection $W^O\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{model}\times d_{model}}$. Key parameter fact: because each head works in a $d_k=d_{model}/h$ subspace, total parameters are ~the same as a single full-width attention — you buy *diversity of relations* at ~no extra parameter cost, only a reshape.

slides.title: The shapes, end to end (h=8, d_model=512)
slides.body: $d_k=512/8=64$. Per head: $Q_t,K_t,V_t$ are $n\times 64$; $\text{head}_t=\text{Attn}(Q_t,K_t,V_t)$ is $n\times 64$. Concatenate 8 heads → $n\times 512$; apply $W^O$ ($512\times512$) → $n\times 512$. Output width equals input width, so blocks stack unchanged. Formally $\text{MultiHead}(X)=\text{Concat}(\text{head}_1,\dots,\text{head}_h)\,W^O$, $\text{head}_t=\text{Attn}(XW^Q_t,XW^K_t,XW^V_t)$. Derive it:

question.question: Derive multi-head attention
question.goal: From: one attention can only average one way — give it several.

steps.prompt: Why multiple heads instead of one big attention?
steps.motivation: Each head attends in its own learned subspace, capturing different relations in parallel.

options: Each head attends in a different learned subspace, in parallel
It is only a speed optimization
It reduces parameters
Heads are identical redundant copies

hints: One softmax can only form one weighting per query.
steps.reveal: h heads = h independent attentions in h subspaces, learned in parallel.

steps.prompt: How are the h head outputs combined?
steps.motivation: Concatenate the per-head outputs and mix them with one output projection.

question.question: You set h=1 with the same total d_model. Versus an h=8 model, what changes?
options: Nothing — multi-head is just a parallelism optimization
8× more parameters
The layer can learn only ONE attention pattern; h=8 could learn up to 8 different patterns at the same capacity
Single-head is strictly better
question.explanation: Same parameter count either way. The value of multi-head is representational diversity: h=8 can simultaneously be a locality head, an induction head, a punctuation head, etc. Collapsing to h=1 forces one pattern and reliably hurts language modeling.

slides.title: A catalog of learned specializations
slides.body: Empirically, trained models grow *reproducible* head types: **previous-token** heads (attend to $i-1$), **positional** heads, **syntactic** heads (verb→subject, noun→determiner), **coreference** heads (pronoun→antecedent), and the celebrated **induction heads** — a two-head circuit implementing "…[A][B]…[A] → predict [B]" that is now believed to be a primary mechanism behind *in-context learning*. The reproducibility of these circuits across models and seeds is the empirical bedrock of mechanistic interpretability; multi-head attention is *why* the model has the capacity to host many such circuits at once.

question.question: An 'induction head' is best described as:
options: A single head that memorizes training sequences
A two-layer circuit (previous-token head → induction head) that completes patterns like 'A B … A → B' — the backbone of in-context learning
The first attention head in layer 0
A head that only attends to punctuation
question.explanation: Induction is compositional: a previous-token head writes 'the token before me' into the residual stream; a later induction head uses that to find the prior occurrence of the current token and attend to whatever followed it. This circuit is strongly linked to in-context learning ability.

slides.title: Grouped-query attention (GQA) and why it exists
slides.body: At inference, autoregressive decoding caches K and V for every past token, every head — the **KV-cache**. Its size $\propto n\cdot h\cdot d_k$ and it dominates memory and bandwidth for long contexts (often *the* serving bottleneck). **Multi-query attention** shares a single K/V across *all* query heads (tiny cache, some quality loss). **Grouped-query attention** is the practical middle: groups of query heads share one K/V head — e.g. 32 query heads → 8 KV heads → 4× smaller cache with near-zero quality loss. This is why Llama-2-70B, Mistral, and most modern served LLMs use GQA. It changes only K/V head count, not the math you derived.

question.question: Why does GQA cut inference memory but leave training cost ≈ unchanged?
options: It only applies at inference; training uses full MHA
It shrinks the KV-cache (built only during autoregressive decoding); forward/backward FLOPs are dominated by matmuls that barely change
It uses lower numerical precision
It runs fewer training steps
question.explanation: GQA's saving is the per-token K/V tensors cached across the context during generation — fewer KV groups ⇒ proportionally smaller cache. Training is FLOP-bound (full sequences, parallel), and those FLOPs are nearly the same, so train cost is ≈ unchanged.

slides.title: The trap: 'just make the one head bigger'
slides.body: A tempting non-fix for "the model can't capture enough relations": keep $h=1$ but enlarge $d_k$ to the full $d_{model}$ (same parameter count). It does **not** help — a single softmax still yields one weighting per query regardless of its dimensionality. Capacity for *simultaneous distinct relations* comes from the *number of heads*, not the width of one. Diagnose:

question.question: Diagnose the quality drop.
question.scenario: A team replaces 8 attention heads of dim 64 with 1 head of dim 512 (identical total parameters). Quality drops on tasks that need several relation types at once.

rubricCriteria.description: a single head produces ONE softmax weighting per query — one relation pattern
it cannot simultaneously attend to e.g. syntax AND coreference
multiple heads attend in parallel independent subspaces, then concat+W^O

question.explanation: Total dimensionality isn't the constraint — number of independent attention patterns is. One head = one weighting; h heads = h patterns in parallel.

hints: One softmax row = one weighting pattern.
Can a single head do syntax AND coreference at once?
slides.workedSolution: A single head emits one softmax weighting per query — one relation. h heads learn h distinct patterns in separate subspaces, recombined by W^O.

question.question: 8 heads of dim 64 vs 1 head of dim 512 (same total dim). The key advantage of 8 heads?
options: It can attend to ~8 different relation patterns in parallel (different subspaces)
It uses fewer parameters
It is always faster
It removes the need for positional encoding
question.explanation: Each head has its own softmax, so it can specialize (one head ~ syntax, another ~ coreference). One big head can only form a single weighting per query.

question.prompt: Explain multi-head attention to your pet.

rubricCriteria.description: each head is attention in its own learned subspace
heads run in parallel capturing different relations
outputs are concatenated then projected by W^O

slides.title: What to carry forward
slides.body: Multi-head = $h$ parallel attentions in $d_{model}/h$ subspaces, concatenated and mixed by $W^O$ — many relations at once for ~the same parameters; GQA shrinks the KV-cache for serving. Attention is now complete. Next: **positional encoding** — restoring order to a permutation-equivariant operation.
